 THIS APPEAL IS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 08.11.2019 passed in MVC No.795/2018 by the Additional Senior Civil Judge, MACT, Srirangapatna (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioner therein have preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.
3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 10.04.2018, at about 11.30 a.m., on Sagar Katte Bridge, Hosakote Mulepetlu Road, Sagarakatte Village, Mysuru, when the petitioner was proceeding on Passion Plus motor bike bearing registration No.KA-05-HJ-8914, at that time, Bajaj CT 100 bike bearing registration No.KA-09-HD-8442, being driven in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against the Passion Plus motor bike due to which the petitioner sustained the following injuries.

sentences.text: Not satisfied by the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
6. Admittedly, the accident occurred in the year 2018.
The income of the petitioner has not been established before the Tribunal.
Hence, the notional income as prescribed in the Lok- Adalath chart has to be considered, which will be Rs.12,500/- per month.
The disability to the whole body is assessed at 15% by the Tribunal.
I deem the same to be just and fair.
The petitioner was aged 46 years at the time of accident.

Hence, the multiplier of 13 has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. D.T.C [2009(6) SCC 121], thus the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.2,92,500/- (Rs.12,500x12x13x15%) towards 'loss of future income' as against Rs.1,75,500/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Given the nature of injuries, the laid up period has to be considered as 3 months and the loss of income during the laid up period will be Rs.37,500/-
(Rs.12,500x3) as against Rs.15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Towards pain and suffering, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.40,000/-.
Towards future medical expenses, based on the actual medical bills, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,34,315/-, I deem the same to be appropriate.

Towards the head 'Food,
diet, Nourishment, Conveyance charges, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.39,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards future medical expenses, a sum of Rs.Rs.10,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to further enhance it to Rs.20,000/-.
Towards loss of amenities, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal, which I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.30,000/-.
Thus, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.7,03,315/- as described in the table below:
